census.popproj2023.reason: Census Bureau population PROJECTIONS (forward vintage popproj2023). census_acs.acs1_2023.reason: American Community Survey 1-year estimates. ACS is a household SAMPLE SURVEY, not an administrative universe, so its aggregates are excluded by principle. cms_nhe.medicaid_title_xix_expenditures.reason: CMS National Health Expenditure Medicaid Title XIX spending. irs_soi.form_w2_designated_roth_401k_con.reason: IRS SOI / W-2 retirement-contribution aggregate. Retirement contributions are modeled as imputed INPUT columns (traditional/roth 401(k) and IRA contributions), governed by the input-coverage contract, not as reweighting targets. Calibrating them as fiscal targets would double-govern a quantity the input-coverage gate already owns.
irs_soi.form_w2_designated_roth_401k_con.evidence: RESTORED_REFERENCE_ECPS_REQUIRED_INPUTS declares the *_contributions_desired input columns in release_input_coverage.py

irs_soi.form_w2_social_security_tips.reason: IRS W-2 Social Security tip aggregates. kff.marketplace_effectuated_enrollment.reason: Kaiser Family Foundation state marketplace effectuated-enrollment compilation. ACA marketplace enrollment is calibrated from the primary CMS administrative source (cms_aca.oep2024, compiled as cms_aca:102); KFF is a secondary aggregator of the same underlying CMS data, excluded to avoid a duplicate target.

usda_snap.national_average_monthly_perso.reason: USDA FNS SNAP average-monthly PERSONS. The SNAP assistance unit is often a subset of the SPM unit (FY2024 FNS persons-per-household 1.88 vs 2.82 simulated members per taker unit), so a person indicator overcounts FNS participants by ~50%. The household caseload (usda_snap.national/state_average_monthly_households, compiled) is the calibrated count; persons stay unmapped until sub-unit participation is modeled.
